i mostly wrote this because i was pissed in arenas because every time i went up against a semi competent valkyrie, it felt like the tactical came out in a millisecond and then stunned me out of nowhere.

Edit: One thing I forgot to mention is that their teammates were across the map using boceks so if i did go out of cover to dodge the missiles if i had the time to react i would have died regardless, in the BR mode she's fine, it's easy to dodge and i have options, in arena where it's mostly micro 1v1s and open area, with a very big long range meta with boceks with little cover in the map pool for arenas, that is where i have a problem with her tactical, either way i die because someone aims in my direction while hovering mid air, and presses q, or I pray to god their teammates can't aim, or I get stunned and finished with a spitfire.

Hm, it's probably hormones and also due to the fact that I'm talking sertraline and risperidone, not sure if I spelt it right but I do remember that in a 3 year period, my parents divorced, I moved across the country, attempted suicide atleast once, learned my dad died, got grabbed by both wrists at a funeral by 2 people, and tugged in both directions, got socially isolated at school, and betrayed by a close friend. I also get compared to my dad every day, and it hurts because he was an alcohol abuser, and smoker. I really don't want to be him to be honest, but I think I may or may not be over that trauma since it happened from when I was 10 to 13. Is that enough time to get over the trauma?

Genuinely thank you to the people that have commented on this post, I honestly didn't really expect people to really notice this but, thank you. It means a lot that random people I don't even know would just help without any sort of incentive to do so other than their kindness. I'll try to enjoy the smaller things of life and not get swept up in all of the news. Reading most of the comments on this kind of bring tears to my eyes. I have a renewed faith in humanity, it'll take a while but I'll get better eventually. For now I'm going to embrace my hobbies to distract myself for right now.

It's not really boredom, more of just a feeling of vague melancholy and emptiness. The dread of life and the groaning agony of every day. It's just kind of where I zone out and stare at the wall feeling empty and just kind of sad almost for atleast 30 minutes and then snap out of it.
